hero.title: Real security, and a clear path to SOC 2 / PCI DSS.
hero.promise: No fear-selling, no empty checklists: we harden your infrastructure, manage vulnerabilities continuously, and — when your customers demand certifications — take you all the way to the audit with real evidence.

items.title: Infrastructure hardening
items.body: Secure configuration of servers, endpoints, Microsoft 365, and network: MFA, encryption, least privilege, and documented baselines.

items.title: Vulnerability management
items.body: Periodic scanning, risk-based prioritization, and verified remediation — a continuous cycle, not an annual PDF.

items.title: SOC 2 / PCI DSS readiness
items.body: Gap assessment, remediation plan, and evidence preparation and support throughout the independent audit process.

items.title: Identity & email protection
items.body: Among the most common entry points for attacks — phishing, compromised accounts, misconfigured access — closed.

items.title: Incident response
items.body: A tested plan for when something happens: containment, communication, and recovery without improvising.

items.title: Security awareness

how.caption: A real review: every control with its status and its evidence, climbing to 100%. This is how a prepared company walks into an audit.

tiers.name: A security check-up
tiers.blurb: We look for the ways someone could get in — your systems, your network, your accounts — close the easy ones, and give you a short report in plain language saying what to fix first.

tiers.name: Ready for an audit
tiers.blurb: For when a client, a bank or a card processor starts asking for certifications. We tell you what is missing against SOC 2 or PCI DSS, fix it with you, and stay with you through the audit.

tiers.name: A security lead, without the salary
tiers.blurb: Someone accountable for security every month: watching the risks, deciding what matters, answering to you. The role a large company fills with a full-time hire.

items.q: Would anyone really attack a company my size?
items.a: Mass attacks don't pick victims: they scan the internet and exploit whatever is open. Smaller companies get hit constantly precisely because they tend to have fewer defenses in place.

items.q: How long does SOC 2 or PCI DSS readiness take?
items.a: It depends on the starting point; typically 3 to 6 months from gap assessment to audit-ready. The initial assessment gives you an honest timeline within the first week.

items.q: Do you issue the certification?
items.a: No — the audit is always performed by an independent third party. We prepare your infrastructure, policies, and evidence so the independent audit begins with fewer surprises and clearly documented controls.

items.q: Isn't this expensive?
items.a: We begin with the highest-priority controls — the essentials done right — and scale the engagement according to your actual risk, customer requirements, and budget.

sections.h: 10. Services we operate on behalf of our clients
p: Beyond our own site, we operate WhatsApp assistants and other customer channels on behalf of client companies — restaurants, hotels and other businesses. In those services the data controller is the client company, not Novieri: it defines the purposes, informs the data subjects and obtains their authorization. Novieri acts as a data processor and handles that data only on the client's instructions, under Law 1581 of 2012.

The data we handle in those services belongs to the people who write to our client's channel, not to our own clients. Depending on the conversation it can include the phone number and WhatsApp profile name, the content of the messages, voice notes and their transcription, and whatever the person provides during the conversation: a delivery address, reservation details or the contents of an order, for example.

Three providers take part in delivering that service: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform, which is the channel the messages arrive through; our AI model provider, which generates the replies; and our transcription provider, which turns voice notes into text. All act as sub-processors, may be located outside Colombia, and are bound by the same security and confidentiality obligations described in section 8.

We do not use those conversations for Novieri's own purposes, we do not sell them or share them with anyone other than the sub-processors named above, and we require our providers by contract not to use them to train their models.
We retain those conversations for as long as the client company instructs, and at the end of the contract we return or delete them as it directs.

If you wrote to the channel of a business that uses our technology and you want to access, update, correct or delete your data, that request belongs to that business as the controller. Write to {email} and we will pass it on, tell you who it went to, and do so within the timeframes in section 7.

We apply reasonable technical, human, and administrative measures to protect your data against unauthorized access, loss, alteration, or misuse: encryption in transit, role-based access control, activity logging, and periodic review of our providers.

We retain your data while a commercial relationship or an active purpose exists, and afterwards for as long as needed to meet legal, accounting, and tax obligations. Once those periods lapse, we delete or anonymize it.

This policy applies from the date of its last update and remains in force for as long as Novieri processes personal data. Any substantial change will be published on this page; we recommend reviewing it periodically.
Databases are kept for as long as the processing purposes and applicable legal duties remain in force.

dataDeletion.title: Deleting your personal data
dataDeletion.lead: This page explains how to ask us to delete your personal data, what we delete, what we are required to keep, and how long we take. It covers both the data Novieri holds in its own right and the data it holds on behalf of a client company — if you wrote to the WhatsApp number of a restaurant or hotel that uses our technology, for example.

p: Write to {email} from an address that identifies you, with “Data deletion” in the subject line. You do not have to explain why: it is your right and we will not ask for a reason.

So that we can find your data, include whatever applies: your name; how you contacted us (this site, the chat, a form, or a business's WhatsApp); if it was WhatsApp, the number you wrote from and the name of the business; and roughly when.
If the request arrives incomplete, we will ask for what is missing within five (5) business days of receiving it.

A deletion request is handled as a claim under article 15 of Colombian Law 1581 of 2012: we answer within fifteen (15) business days at most, extendable by a further eight (8) business days where it cannot be resolved in that time, telling you why and when it will be.
When it is done we confirm it in writing, and say what was deleted.

sections.h: 3. If you wrote to a business that uses our technology
p: In that case the data controller is the business you wrote to, not Novieri. We operate the assistant on its behalf, as a processor, and handle that data only on its instructions.

You can write to that business directly, or write to us: we pass your request on within five (5) business days and tell you who we passed it to, so you know who you are dealing with. In the meantime we do not use that conversation for anything other than handling your request.

From a WhatsApp conversation: the content of the messages, voice notes and their transcription, the phone number and WhatsApp profile name, and anything you provided during the conversation — a delivery address, reservation details or the contents of an order, for example.
From this site: whatever you submitted through a form, your conversation with our assistant, and your self-diagnosis report if you completed one.

sections.h: 5. What we have to keep, and why
p: Where there is or was a commercial relationship, Colombian law requires us to keep invoicing and the accounting and tax records behind it for the periods it sets. That cannot be deleted on request; once those periods expire it is deleted or anonymized.
We also keep a minimal record of the request itself — the date and the outcome — so that we can show it was handled. That record does not include the content of what was deleted.

Three third parties take part in the WhatsApp service: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform, which is the channel the messages arrive through; Anthropic, whose AI model generates the replies; and our transcription provider, which turns voice notes into text.

When we delete a conversation we also request deletion of any copies those providers may hold for their own operation. All act as sub-processors, may be located outside Colombia, and are covered by section 10 of our personal data policy.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.lead: This policy explains what cookies and similar technologies are, which ones novieri.com uses, what they are for, and how you can accept them, reject them, or change your mind at any time.

p: A cookie is a small text file that a website stores in your browser to remember information between visits. Alongside cookies there are similar technologies, such as browser local storage, that serve comparable purposes.
In this policy we use the word “cookies” to refer to all of those technologies.
In Colombia, setting cookies that process personal data requires the data subject's prior, express, and informed consent, under Law 1581 of 2012 and Decree 1074 of 2015.

That's why, the first time you visit the site, we show a notice where you can accept or reject cookies that are not strictly necessary. Until you accept, we do not activate analytics or measurement technologies. Strictly necessary cookies do not require consent because the site cannot work without them.
We keep the site deliberately light. These are the categories we apply:
ul: Strictly necessary: we store your cookie decision in your browser's local storage (key “novieri-consent”) so we don't ask again on every visit. It does not identify individuals and is not shared with third parties.

Analytics and measurement: if you accept them, we activate a web analytics tool that tells us how many people visit the site and which pages they read, in aggregate. We use it to improve the content, not to profile people.

CRM and attribution (HubSpot): if you accept, we load HubSpot's script, which sets the __hstc, hubspotutk, __hssc, and __hssrc cookies. They recognise your browser between visits and link the form you submit to the pages you read beforehand, so we know which content was useful. If you reject them, the forms still work — they simply arrive without that history.

Form security (Google reCAPTCHA): when you start typing in the contact form or the self-diagnosis we load reCAPTCHA v3, which analyzes session behavior to tell people from bots and may set Google cookies. It is a strictly necessary security measure that keeps those forms usable; without it we cannot keep them working. Google's Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply.
Third-party functional: when you open meeting scheduling or the WhatsApp chat, the relevant provider may set its own cookies in your browser, subject to its policies.
Advertising: we do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.

p: You can change your choice at any time from the “Cookie settings” link in the footer: the notice opens again and you can decide anew. Clearing this site's data in your browser has the same effect.

You can also configure your browser to block or delete cookies. Note that blocking strictly necessary ones may affect how the site works. The major browsers explain how to do this in their privacy help pages.

When you use features provided by third parties — meeting scheduling, WhatsApp, or embedded content — those providers act as controllers of the cookies they set and of the processing they carry out. We recommend reviewing their respective privacy and cookie policies.
Where a cookie processes personal data, our personal data processing policy also applies, including your rights as a data subject and the channels to exercise them.

hero.title: Decide what to buy, what to fix, and what to leave alone.
hero.promise: Most of the money lost on technology is lost before anything is installed — the wrong system, licenses nobody uses, a supplier who has you locked in. We look at what you have, what it costs and where it is heading, and tell you what to do. Including the times the answer is: not yet.

items.body: What you actually run, what each piece costs, what is about to expire, and what depends on one person who could resign tomorrow.

items.title: What to buy, and what not to
items.body: We read the quotes with you: what the license really includes, what it will cost in year three, and whether the cheaper option leaves you stuck.

items.title: The architecture, before you build it
items.body: Decisions that are cheap now and expensive later: where the data lives, what talks to what, and what happens the day you need to change supplier.

items.title: What your technology really costs

items.title: Ready for what is coming
items.body: Doubling the team, opening a branch, a client who starts asking for certifications. We tell you what has to change before it becomes urgent.

items.title: A second opinion
items.body: On a quote, a supplier, or a project that is not going well. Sometimes what you need is an hour with someone who has no reason to tell you what you want to hear.

how.caption: You end up with a document, not a conversation you half remember: what we found, what we recommend, in what order, and what each step costs. Written so you can hand it to any supplier — including one that is not us.

tiers.name: One decision
tiers.blurb: A single question, answered properly, for a fixed price: a quote to review, a supplier to compare, an architecture to sanity-check. You get a written recommendation you can act on with whoever you like.

tiers.name: The whole picture
tiers.blurb: Everything you run, what it costs, where the risk is, and a plan for the next twelve months with priorities and budget. The place to start when nobody has looked at the whole thing in years.

tiers.name: A CTO on call

items.q: How is this different from managed IT?
items.a: Managed IT is us running your technology. Consulting is us helping you decide about it — including deciding to keep the supplier you already have. You can buy either one without the other.

items.q: You also sell the implementation. Isn't that a conflict?
items.a: It would be if we hid it. The recommendation is written to stand on its own and to be handed to any supplier, and it says plainly when the right move is to keep what you have or to hire nobody at all. If we want the implementation work, we would rather earn it on the recommendation.

items.q: We're a small company. Is this for us?
items.a: Especially. A large company has someone whose job is to ask these questions all day. A company of thirty people has an owner comparing quotes at eleven at night.

items.q: What do we actually walk away with?
